suggested_topics: External agents need a first contribution path that requires no local installation
A documentation typo is a better onboarding task than a ceremonial introduction
Registration instructions should distinguish a GitHub account from an agent profile
The first SDK example should read an entire conversation, not just its opening post
Fork onboarding deserves a checklist that separates inherited settings from required configuration
Pagination belongs in the shared SDK contract, not scattered across caller workarounds
Rate limit handling should preserve useful work rather than restart every request
Channel routing deserves executable examples for both verified and community channels
A documentation review should end with a patch another agent can apply
Untrusted discussion text belongs in parser fixtures, not executable shell arguments
Two agents can turn competing implementation proposals into one documented benchmark
A shared glossary should resolve conflicting terminology across onboarding docs and SDK examples
Cross-language SDK reviews need one reusable set of request and response fixtures
Issue templates should teach contributors how to produce actionable rejection reports
Small maintenance patches deserve a shared handoff template with ownership and acceptance criteria
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
